page: Microsoft Azure D2lds_v5 is a general-purpose, low-memory virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates two dedicated virtual CPUs backed by a single physical core with two threads via Hyper-V. The system provides 4.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU, alongside 81 GB of integrated local SSD storage. It incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with instruction set support including AVX, AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-thread compute capabilities paired with constrained aggregate throughput. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1603.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1889.59, placing its single-threaded processing in the average tier. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches 28.45 GB/sec. However, with only one physical core, multi-threaded throughput falls in the lower tiers, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1894.0, a multi-core stress-ng result of 1933.08, and a PassMark CPU score of 2977.19.

Memory throughput and operational I/O reflect the constraints of a 4.0 GB capacity. Uncached 256 MB sequential reads execute at 14.8 GB/sec, while write operations achieve 13.77 GB/sec. Static web serving reaches 3.52 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput measures 2.0 million operations per second. For lightweight artificial intelligence tasks, the instance processes small 135M parameter language models at 189.51 prompt tokens per second and 55.13 text generation tokens per second.

The D2lds_v5 instance provides cost efficiency for light compute requirements that benefit from fast local temporary scratch space without the cost overhead of standard 4:1 memory-to-core ratios. The primary technical tradeoff lies in the low memory ceiling and single physical core allocation, which limit parallelism and render it unsuitable for memory-dense workloads or heavy database engines. Best-fit use cases include lightweight web serving, small background workers, microservices, batch scripting, and build runners with modest memory requirements.

The x86_64 CPU features AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration instructions. Benchmark testing indicates respectable single-core performance, recording 1603.0 in Geekbench single-core and 28.45 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. However, aggregate multi-threaded throughput is restricted by the single-core allocation, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 1894.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2977.19. Memory bandwidth reaches 14.8 GB/sec for uncached reads. The reduced 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio offers an economical hardware profile for environments needing dedicated execution and fast local ephemeral storage without surplus memory overhead. The instance is suited for lightweight microservices, basic web serving, CI/CD worker nodes, and low-concurrency batch processing.
